standard_prerequisites.name: The two-term presentation of the naive cotangent complex of a quotient of a polynomial algebra
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the representing complex whose amplitude is to be bounded.

standard_prerequisites.name: The criterion that a complex with finite free last term has tor amplitude in a range if and only if the previous term is flat
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the amplitude condition to flatness of the conormal module.

standard_prerequisites.name: A quasi-regular ideal has finite projective conormal module
standard_prerequisites.use: Upgrades flatness to finite projectivity, giving perfectness.

standard_prerequisites.name: A Koszul regular ideal is quasi-regular
standard_prerequisites.use: Connects the definition of local complete intersection to the quasi-regularity input.

core_obligations: Write B = A[x_1, ..., x_n]/I and represent NL_{B/A} by the complex I/I^2 -> bigoplus B dx_i with I/I^2 placed in degree -1 (proof lines 22864-22869).

Use that the degree 0 term is finite free and the statement on the last term being flat to conclude that the complex has tor amplitude in [-1, 0] if and only if I/I^2 is a flat B-module (proof lines 22869-22872).
Use that I is Koszul regular by definition, hence quasi-regular by the cited section (proof lines 22872-22873).
Apply the quasi-regular ideal statement to conclude that I/I^2 is a finite projective B-module, giving both perfectness of NL_{B/A} and tor amplitude in [-1, 0] (proof lines 22874-22877).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a local complete intersection A -> B in the sense of the local complete intersection definition and asserts that the naive cotangent complex NL_{B/A} is a perfect object of D(B) with tor amplitude in [-1, 0] (source lines 22855-22861). The proof exhibits the standard two-term presentation: write B = A[x_1, ..., x_n]/I, so that NL_{B/A} is represented by the complex I/I^2 -> bigoplus B dx_i with I/I^2 in degree -1 (proof lines 22864-22869). Since the degree 0 term is finite free, the amplitude statement is equivalent to flatness of I/I^2 as a B-module, by the lemma on the last term being flat (proof lines 22869-22872). By definition I is a Koszul regular ideal and hence quasi-regular (proof lines 22872-22873). It follows from the quasi-regular ideal statement that I/I^2 is a finite projective B-module, so NL_{B/A} is both perfect and of tor amplitude in [-1, 0] (proof lines 22874-22877). The non-routine content is the reduction of the amplitude question to flatness of the conormal module via the freeness of the degree 0 term, and the conversion of quasi-regularity into finite projectivity of I/I^2.
